linkedin.post:
For the SatForge UAE 2026 National University Satellite Engineering Challenge (Qualifiers), my team, Team Kanban, designed MARSAD-1 (مرصد, Arabic for "observatory"): a 3U CubeSat in a 550 km sun-synchronous orbit that watches the UAE coast for harmful algal blooms.

Why: in 2008-2009 a red tide lasted months, killed fish and forced desalination plants to cut output, and desalination supplies most of the UAE's drinking water. MARSAD-1 computes a chlorophyll index (NDCI) on board and only downlinks alerts.

What we built: the mission design and budgets (3.92 W load vs 6.6 W generated, 0.845 of 4 kg, 1,420 of 3,000 AED), a Tinkercad circuit of the flight logic, a 3D model, a live mission-control dashboard with fault-injection tests, an A2 poster, a 16-page technical report, a demo video and a recorded presentation.

Honest note: the lab and orbit shots in this reel are AI visualisations of the planned build. The ESP32-S3 flight firmware is written; the physical board is next.

Built with Mohammad Umar (power/EPS), Bilal Feroz (attitude control, structure, 3D design) and Maryam Alnaqbi (payload, comms, bloom science), with me, Awaiz Ahmed, on mission lead, flight software and the dashboard.

Live dashboard: https://4waiz.github.io/marsad-1-dashboard
Code: https://github.com/4waiz/marsad-1-dashboard

honesty.ai_visualisations: Vidu AI clips (v1_bench, v3_antenna, v5_orbit_open, v6_orbit_close) and the ChatGPT stills they were made from; labelled AI VISUALISATION on screen
honesty.real_recordings: dash_rec.mp4 (live dashboard + fault injection, sped up) and sim.mp4 (Tinkercad simulation, 1.5x); labelled REAL RECORDING on screen
honesty.illustrative: the reflectance curves in the spectral-sensor card (shape only, labelled illustrative); the coast/plant and watchtower drawings
honesty.not_claimed: the physical board is not built yet; the ESP32-S3 firmware is written

script: A *red tide* can cut off the water you drink.
Most UAE drinking water comes from *desalination* plants.
In 2008, a red tide lasted *months*,
killed fish, and forced plants to cut output.
Picture a *watchtower* keeper on the coast.
He spots it *early*, before it reaches the intake.
We put that keeper in *orbit*.
Meet *Marsad One*, a CubeSat 550 kilometres up.
Its eyes compare red-edge and red light:
a *chlorophyll* index, computed on board.
It only sends down *alerts*, like the keeper's flag.
Power, mass and cost all fit, with *room* to spare.
We wired the flight logic as a *Tinkercad* circuit.
5 seconds after boot, the *antenna* deploys.
Each shot began as a rough *still*,
then became an AI visualisation.
The keeper's logbook is our live *mission control*.
We break it on purpose: low battery turns it *red*,
and a lost link goes stale, then recovers.
Plus a 3D model, a poster, a report and a *demo*.
Built by Team *Kanban*: Awaiz, Umar, Bilal and Maryam.
The real flight board is *next*.
Spot the red early...
*protect* the water.
